summary_en: Japan Ecosystem will acquire up to 350,000 shares (3.97% of outstanding shares) from Shoufuku Co., Ltd., the controlling shareholder, for a maximum of ¥700 million through private negotiation. The acquisition price will be the lower of the previous day's closing price or the two-month average closing price, each multiplied by 0.95, with settlement on December 24, 2026, subject to shareholder approval.
title_en: Notice Regarding Acquisition of Treasury Shares from a Specific Shareholder
translation_en_brief:
On November 20, 2026, Japan Ecosystem announced its intention to acquire up to 350,000 treasury shares from Shoufuku Co., Ltd., its controlling shareholder holding 37.46% of voting rights as of September 30, 2026. The transaction will be conducted through private negotiation rather than open market purchase to minimize market impact. The maximum acquisition cost is ¥700 million, with per-share price calculated as the lower of two figures: (1) the closing price on December 22, 2026 (the day before the shareholder meeting) multiplied by 0.95, or (2) the average closing price over the preceding two months multiplied by 0.95. Settlement will occur on December 24, 2026.

The company emphasized that the acquisition price will not exceed the statutory market price threshold defined under the Companies Act Article 161, and that it maintains financial soundness after the acquisition. The board determined the transaction satisfies capital efficiency objectives while protecting minority shareholders' interests. The acquisition requires approval by special resolution at the ordinary general meeting scheduled for December 23, 2026, at which point Shoufuku will be unable to vote on this agenda item pursuant to Companies Act Article 160(4). Five independent outside directors and audit committee members reviewed the transaction and confirmed its rationality and that transaction terms are appropriate without harming minority shareholders.

Representative Director Shigeru Matsushima holds the dual position of both Japan Ecosystem's CEO and Shoufuku's representative director, making Shoufuku a related party under the company's Related Party Management Regulations. The company stated it will consider future capital allocation uses for the acquired shares.
